Same machinery behaviour attempt-1 recorded (`sig-2026-11-20.1` stranded the same way) — the allocation writes before the build completes, so an auto-allocated build can never close on a ~hour-long build. Side-effect recorded, never hidden: `labels.json` carries a second stranded allocation `sig-2026-11-25.1` (`state=allocated`, `publication_id=null`); the build's lock stayed held `{verb=build, acquired_at=16:41:09Z}`. |
| 17:52 | `release build --apply` retry (`--label sig-2026-11-25.1 --environment production --break-lock "stale build lock from the 16:41Z auto-allocation run…"`) | **applied** — naming the already-allocated label skips `_allocate_label`, so no registry state moves under the lock; `built` journaled (000007). ~52 min build. The refused first tree (`/private/tmp/sig-p3765a/work-refused-stalegen`, pub `p-00c22ef8…`) is kept as residue — `built_at` rides the hashed descriptor, so a rebuild mints a different pub and the trees can never share a work dir. |

A `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token` subprocess exceeded the client's 15s timeout under load → `default_token_provider()` returned `None` → unhandled `GcsError` ended the verb at **8/462,497 objects**. The lock stayed held (`{verb:"stage", acquired_at:"2026-11-25T19:41:59Z", holder:"local", registry_state_sha256:"64e87456…"}` — the forensic record; `--break-lock` is the recorded override) and the 8 residue objects under `staged/r/p-31371dfb…/` are create-if-absent, byte-identical — a resume skips them. |

## Web dist builds — verified bound `ERR_STRING_TOO_LONG` (the leg's hard stop)

Both export-mode Astro builds ran against `SIG_EXPORT_DIR=exports/out/national`
(the `v/` latest-view dist at `web/dist`, `06-dist-latest.log`, started
~12:52 ET; the `s/<pub>` snapshot dist at `/private/tmp/sig-p3765a/dist-snap`,
`10-dist-snap.log`, started ~14:05 ET). Neither ever emitted a page: both
were still in `generating static routes` (the getStaticPaths phase —
each of the ~15 entity route files re-runs `entityIndex(getEntityLabelRows())`,
re-parsing the 143 MB / 260,822-row `labels/*.jsonl` corpus per call plus a
`readdirSync` per entity key) when this leg was recorded (build 1 at
T+~3.2 h, 0 routes emitted).

The bound underneath is verified, not projected. `getStatementIndex()`
(`web/src/lib/data.ts:2029`) loads every `<comp>/statements.jsonl` with
`readFileSync(p, "utf-8")`; `osm_physical/statements.jsonl` is
**1,013,125,905 bytes** — over V8's `0x1fffffe8` (536,870,376-char) string
cap — so the call throws `Error: Cannot create a string longer than
0x1fffffe8 characters`. Reproduced verbatim through the package's own
harness (`vitest`, pinned node v24.21.0, `SIG_DATA_SOURCE=export` —
the throw at `data.ts:2029` after ~13 s) and by direct
`readFileSync` under the same node. The first rendered page that calls
`getStatementIndex()` — `entity/[type]/[key]/index.astro:111`,
`evidence/claim/[id].astro:63`, `explore/index.astro:150`,
`disagreements/*`, `watch/item/[handle].astro:56` — kills the whole build.
Both dist builds will exit non-zero with this error whenever their
getStaticPaths phase ends; they were left running at leg-record time so
their own logs carry the crash too.

Second, deeper bound (recorded, even if the string cap were lifted): the
data layer is **non-memoized** — every one of ~258k entity pages re-parses
the full ~1.9 GB statements corpus (`getStatementIndex()` line 111,
unconditional) and rebuilds `getRecordBasisIndex()` **per claim** (line
113). That is O(corpus) per route — quadratic; no streaming fix alone
makes the entity dist build feasible. `D-P37.65a-2` records the owed work.

`sites` was therefore **never invoked** — `--latest-dist`/`--snapshot-dist`
name the two dists and the verb would have journaled a `sites` event over
whatever partial trees existed; running it would fabricate a sites record.

## Stage leg — measured bound + machinery stop (verbatim)

- Dry-run: `release stage --work-dir /private/tmp/sig-p3765a/work` →
  `plan: insert 462497 objects under staged/*/p-31371dfb…/` — the `r/` +
  `releases/` residue only (the `v/`/`s/` trees `sites` would emit do not
  exist). With both dists + ~226k stubs the full plan would be ~700k.
- `--apply` started ~19:38Z; plan scan ~3.5 min; lock acquired 19:41:59Z.
  Measured: 8 objects in ~9.6 min of loop time ≈ **0.014 obj/s**
  (attempt-1 measured ~0.37 obj/s on this registry; the difference is the
  per-request `gcloud` ADC token subprocess — **5–6 s wall each**, measured
  ×2 — where the sig-release job on GCP resolves off the metadata server).
  Per object: 1 `store.insert` + `lock.refresh()` = ~7 serial GCS
  JSON-API calls ⇒ ~40–60 s/object under local ADC.
- The verb **died on its own** at ~19:51–55Z — verbatim `GcsError` above —
  a token call exceeding its 15 s timeout is a hard exit, not a retry.
  The machinery's own boundary, recorded, never smoothed.
- Projection at the measured rate: 462,497 objects ≈ **~380 days**; at
  attempt-1's 0.37 obj/s ≈ ~14.5 d for the partial plan, ~22 d full —
  infeasible in-window either way, and the real plan is the full one.
  `D-P37.65a-3` records the owed machinery work (parallel insert /
  amortised digest / cached-or-metadata token / retry on transient
  token failure).

## live-crawl leg — never reached

`release verify --mode S` requires a staged candidate + the IAM-only
origin; the `staged` event never emitted. Recorded, never smoothed:
even a completed stage would hit V14 (no prior `latest.json` — the first
release ever) and V15 (no `sig.quality-report/1` exists — P37.67's leg)
as blocking skips under SIG-ENG-042, exactly as attempt-1 recorded.
